definitions.gloss: Tanabata decorations; ornamental strips and streamers for the Star Festival
definitions.explanation: Colorful paper decorations — primarily {短冊|たんざく} (paper strips with wishes), origami cranes, and streamers — hung on bamboo branches for the July 7 Tanabata festival.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}りを{作|つく}る。
{商店街|しょうてんがい}に{七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}りが{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Tanabata decorations are lined up along the shopping street.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{短冊|たんざく}に{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{書|か}いて{七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}りに{結|むす}んだ。
examples.english: The children wrote their wishes on paper strips and tied them to the Tanabata decorations.

notes:
Compound of {七夕|たなばた} (Star Festival, July 7) + {飾|かざ}り (decoration). Refers collectively to the bamboo-and-paper decorations displayed in homes, schools, train stations, and shopping districts.

COMMON COMPONENTS:
- {短冊|たんざく}: paper strips inscribed with wishes
- {折|お}り{鶴|づる}: origami cranes
- {吹|ふ}き{流|なが}し: streamers
- {笹|ささ}{飾|かざ}り: bamboo decoration (alternative name)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Tanabata legend tells of two stars — Orihime and Hikoboshi — who can meet only once a year across the Milky Way. People write wishes on {短冊|たんざく} hoping the stars will grant them. The Sendai Tanabata Festival is famous for its elaborate displays.
